newsitem.title: KENYA: RALLYING-COLIN MCRAE HEADING FOR SAFARI RALLY VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-COLIN MCRAE HEADING FOR SAFARI RALLY VICTORY.

text.p: Briton Colin McRae was heading for victory in the Safari Rally on Monday after second-placed Richard Burns's team said they would not be pushing to close the gap on the Subaru driver.

McRae, who has claimed only one fourth place finish in two rounds of the championship so far this year, maintained his overnight margin of five minutes over Burns throughout the morning's three stages despite suffering electrical problems on his car.
Burns, whose Mitsubishi has clutch problems, was unaware that McRae was having difficulties but his co-driver Robert Reid said that they would accept their second position.
"Our strategy had been to go like hell on the first stage and then let it be," he said. "We are just going at our own pace, staying out of trouble and guarding second place."
Kenyan Ian Duncan maintained his third position but dropped back from the leading duo after suffering drive shaft problems and losing his rear windscreen.

German Armin Schwarz, the only other world championship contender left in the rally, had a miserable 10th stage when he stalled his car in a sand drift and also burnt his arm slightly while repairing a loose starter motor.

With one stage to go, the 155-km run from Oltepesi to Olepolos, McRae only needs to stay out of trouble to be assured of his first win of the season and move to the head of the world championship table.
